note: Two kinds of copy are declared here, on the estate's copy registry (`roadmapctl copies <workspace-root>`), so that a copy that has drifted from its source is named on the sweep before anyone meets a red gate they did not cause. (1) `records` — the conformance families this repository EMITS and the shared wire-format corpus carries a declared copy of (Phase 172): `conformance/laws/transform-laws.json` and the `conformance/apply/` pair are authored HERE, the default suite certifies the committed files, and the corpus copies are what the five hosts read at the same paths with the same bytes. `check` is `fingerprint` because the two repositories may legitimately differ in end-of-line policy and nothing else; the `regen` writes the copy with the same exporter that writes the source, from the workspace root. The corpus's own `copies.json` is generated and co-owned by the ts/py bundlers and is not edited: the registry walks ANY `copies.json`, so the producer declares in its own file. (2) `$sources` — the proof-leg kit (proofs/kit/, Phase 155), a scaffold other repositories adopt BY COPY; no adopter exists yet, see `$adoptionStatus`. Since Phase 175 the set also carries the MODELS under `proofs/` — the generic theorems (`DagFold`, `Chain`, `WireCanon`, `WireDecode`, `JsonParse`, `Limits`), the reference instance a domain instantiates against (`TreeOps`, `Skeleton`, `Preservation`, `TreeDiff`) and the instantiation template — each entry saying which theorem it carries and which obligations it asks a domain for; the sources ARE the live files, so there is no second copy of any model in this repository. Not in the set: `Vocabulary.fst`, generated from THIS repository's `idl.json`, and `WireVersioning.fst`, a theorem about this repository's IDL diff (Phase 151) — an adopter with an IDL of its own takes that up when its shape is measured. `$sources` is inert data the registry ignores; an adopter's record is that shape with one path filled in, and it moves into `records` the moment a real copy exists.
$adoptionStatus: Measured 2026-09-15, across the whole workspace: exactly ONE proof leg exists — this repository's. No other repository holds a `check.ps1`, an `fstar-pin.json`, a `proofs/` directory or a `.fst` model. The phase that cut this kit was written against the expectation that three consumers (the program tier, the app-composition tier, the remoting decoder) had already copied the leg by hand and that the pin was therefore four numbers; they had not and it was not. The kit is still the right artefact — a scaffold shipped once is worth the same before the first adopter as after — but the drift half has nothing to check yet, and declaring records for copies that do not exist would put a permanent finding on every workspace sweep about an adoption nobody has scheduled. Each adopter appends its own record, from `$sources`, in the change-set that adopts.
